html:
SMTO-RST-0009 — This task can't continue with different settings

GUID: cb9aac13-3ec8-487d-8d9b-23555d026fb7
Slug: resume-snapshot-mismatch
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • SMTO saves the model, Gateways (the helper programs that run commands on your computers) and permissions a task started with. It can't continue the task with different or incomplete settings, so the task didn't continue.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you changed the model, Gateways or permissions since the task started, change them back, then select Resume or Continue task. The task can only continue with the same settings it started with.
  2. If you need the new settings, first read the old task's results to see which steps already finished. Check whether the earlier action already happened, so a new task doesn't repeat it.
  3. Then send a new message with the new settings that describes only what's still left to do. A new task saves its own settings, so they don't have to match the old task's.

What success looks like

  • The task continues with its original settings, or a new task runs without this error and doesn't redo finished work.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before you try anything again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; the details say which saved setting didn't match. Don't edit saved task data to make the settings match.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A resume or task attempt changed the run's captured model routing, authority, redaction or guard policy, or the saved snapshot is missing required fields (including older event and Memory-learning formats), so SnapshotIntegrityError rejected it.

What this means

  • Resume/snapshot checks find changed captured authority/model/policy or missing required snapshot fields, including historical event and Memory-learning identity formats. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Resume/snapshot checks find changed captured authority/model/policy or missing required snapshot fields, including historical event and Memory-learning identity formats.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare current intent with the accepted snapshot; distinguish changed settings from missing historical fields.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the SnapshotIntegrityError message and the native.state.missing_current_snapshot log line to see which captured field differs or is missing. Resume with the original saved snapshot; for changed settings, start a new task grounded in the retained results and reconcile prior effects before requesting mutations.
  • Resume with the original saved configuration. For changed settings, start a new task grounded in retained results and reconcile prior effects before requesting mutations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original supported snapshot is used, or a new task explicitly captures intended changes after prior effects are reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
